title: Sharing equally
examples: Teacher, what does it mean to share fairly?
If I have ten crayons and share them among four friends, what happens?
Can you show me how to find the leftovers when I share?

explain.say: Sharing equally means everyone gets the same amount. Here are four apples for two children.
Give one apple to each child in turn. Keep going until all the apples are shared. Each child gets two.
You can also make groups. Put six stickers in groups of two. You make three groups.
Sometimes some things are left over. Share seven crayons between three friends. Each friend gets two, and one crayon is left over.

faq.q: What does it mean to share fairly?
faq.a: It means that every person gets the exact same amount of things. If you share five toys between two friends, each friend gets two toys with one left over.
asks: How do I make sure everyone gets the same amount?

faq.q: How do I know how many groups I can make?
faq.a: You count how many items you have and then count how many items you want in each group. For example, ten items in groups of five make two groups.
asks: Can I make groups of four from twelve?

faq.q: What are leftovers when I share?
faq.a: Leftovers are the things left after you share as much as you can. If you share ten things among three people, each gets three and one is left over.
asks: What is the remainder when sharing?
Why are there extra things left?

faq.q: Can I share things that are not whole numbers?
faq.a: At first, you share whole things like apples or crayons. Sharing parts of things comes later in maths.
asks: Can we share a pizza equally?

faq.q: If I share twelve between three, how many does each get?
faq.a: You give one to the first person, one to the second, and one to the third. You keep doing this until all twelve are gone. Each person gets four.
asks: How many in each group of three?

facts: Sharing equally means dividing things into equal parts.
When we group things, we count how many sets we can make.
Leftovers are the items that cannot be shared equally.
If you share ten items among five friends, everyone gets two.

quiz.say: Share 8 pencils between 4 friends. Tap how many each gets.
quiz.why: Give one pencil to each friend, two times round. Each friend gets two.

wrong.1: After one round, four pencils are still left to share.
wrong.2: Four is the number of friends, and each friend gets two pencils.

quiz.say: Put 10 balloons in groups of 2. Tap how many groups.
quiz.why: Count in twos: two, four, six, eight, ten. That makes five groups.

wrong.0: Two is the size of each group, so count the groups.
wrong.2: Ten is all the balloons, so count the groups of two.

quiz.say: Share 12 grapes between 4 friends. Tap how many each gets.
quiz.why: Give one grape to each friend, three times round. Each friend gets three.

wrong.0: Four is the number of friends, and each friend gets three.
wrong.1: After two rounds, four grapes are still left to share.
